function: Channel prediction (CNN-LSTM) and outage-constrained multibeam precoding (DNN) for downlink LEO satellite IoT, with VAE channel-error augmentation (p. 1, p. 3).
system: LEO satellite with uniform circular array of M=16 antennas, K=16 single-antenna IoT devices, downlink, 5 GHz carrier, 1000 km orbit, 25 MHz; no RIS (p. 3, p. 9).
method: Supervised CNN-LSTM channel predictor; unsupervised CNN-FC precoder trained with a quantile-penalty loss for outage-constrained weighted sum rate; VAE-based channel error augmentation (p. 4, p. 6, p. 7).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician LEO channel with rain fading, Doppler, delay; parameters per 3GPP TR 38.821; 16000 training, 4000 test samples for prediction (p. 9, p. 10).
test_conditions: Same simulator for training and testing (held-out samples); sweeps over input step size, carrier frequency, altitude, antennas, devices, power; no model tested in unseen conditions (p. 10-13).
baselines: Prediction: linear regression [1], LSTM [18], RNN [32], random forest [33]; precoding: MLP [24], DDPG [34], BTI [35], ZFBF [36]; non-robust and Gaussian-error robust schemes (p. 10-13).
metrics: NMSE of predicted CSI; weighted sum rate; outage probability; execution time; training and validation loss (p. 10-13).
complexity: Order of complexity of the CNN-LSTM predictor and CNN-FC precoder (Section IV-D); average execution time versus antennas and devices against four baselines (p. 9, p. 11-12).
openness: none; trained with open-source TensorFlow but no code or data link given (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 9: "The main simulation system parameters for LEO satellite IoT is set up according to 3GPP TR 38.821"; the channel itself is the authors' own Rician model of Eqs. (1)-(6) (p. 3), not the TR 38.811 or 38.901 model.
q2_support: p. 10: "number of training samples and testing samples are set as 16000 and 4000, respectively"; only held-out samples and sweeps (Fig. 10 varies fc and d0); no model trained in one setting is tested in another.
q3_support: p. 11: "the MLP scheme proposed in [24], the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) scheme in [34], the Bernstein-type inequality (BTI) scheme in [35], and the zero-forcing beamforming (ZFBF) scheme in [36]"; p. 12: "the WSR performance of the proposed scheme is slightly worse than BTI scheme but is much better than other two schemes".
q4_support: p. 9: "we analyze the computational complexity of the two proposed DL-based networks, i.e., DLPDN and DLPCN"; p. 11: "we adopt the average execution time as the metric to measure the computational complexity performance".
q5_support: p. 9: "The estimated CSI dataset is generated according to (8)"; p. 11: "The whole model is trained with the open-source machine learning framework Tensorflow 2.11.0"; no code or data link.
notes: Area 6: the learned multibeam precoding and the channel prediction serve a LEO satellite link, and the more specific area wins over 2 and 3. The channel is the authors' own Rician, Doppler and rain model (p. 3); only the system parameters of Table I follow 3GPP TR 38.821 (p. 9), so q1 is not met, and the reviewer should confirm. q3 met by ZFBF and BTI (non-learned) with MLP, DDPG, LSTM and RNN (learned), compared on WSR or NMSE (p. 10-12).
